src/storage/mod.rs now contains the Storage trait, IMPLEMENTED VERBATIM AS
FROZEN in docs/quern.md §3. Nothing added, nothing removed, no `schema()`
method (bead .42: exec-dml takes `&Schema` as a parameter). Committed on its
own so you are unblocked on the signatures before my `Db` lands.

    pub trait Storage {
        fn create_table(&mut self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<()>;
        fn drop_table(&mut self, table: &str) -> Result<()>;
        fn insert(&mut self, table: &str, row: &Row) -> Result<RowId>;
        fn delete(&mut self, table: &str, id: RowId) -> Result<()>;
        fn update(&mut self, table: &str, id: RowId, row: &Row) -> Result<()>;
        fn scan(&self, table: &str) -> Result<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = Result<(RowId, Row)>> + '_>>;
        fn lookup_pk(&self, table: &str, key: i64) -> Result<Option<(RowId, Row)>>;
        fn begin(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
        fn commit(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
        fn rollback(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
    }

ONE THING I HAD TO ADD, AND IT IS NOT A CONTRACT CHANGE: `#[allow(clippy::
type_complexity)]` sits on `scan`. `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` rejects
that return type outright ("very complex type used"), and a type alias would
change the frozen spelling. If you write the same type in your own file you
will need the same allow — that is clippy, not a broken signature.

WHAT §3 MEANS FOR YOUR CODE (bead .35, and it is a hard borrow rule, not advice)

`scan(&self)` returns a boxed iterator with `+ '_`, so it holds an immutable
borrow of the whole Storage for as long as it lives. Therefore:

  - You CANNOT mutate while a scan is alive. `for r in s.scan("t")? {
    s.update(..) }` is E0502 and no implementation can fix it.
  - exec-dml: collect the `(RowId, Row)` hits into a Vec, DROP the iterator,
    then mutate. Two phases, in that order.
  - exec-scan / plan-physical: a constructor that materialises rows and ends
    the borrow is the only shape that survives `fn build(s: &dyn Storage)`.
  - `Box<dyn Iterator + '_>` means `&dyn Storage` works fine; no generics
    needed anywhere.

WHAT `Db` (landing next, same file) WILL DO BEHIND EACH METHOD — code against
the trait, but these are the semantics you will observe:

  - `Db::open(&Path)` -> `Result<Db>`: takes the DATABASE DIRECTORY (bead .37:
    <db-dir>/quern.db + <db-dir>/quern.wal, created if missing), replays the
    WAL, re-applies committed records, flushes, then checkpoints.
  - `insert` on a table with an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY writes the heap AND the
    btree. A duplicate key is `Err(QuernError::Type("duplicate PRIMARY KEY
    value {k} in table {t}"))` — the btree signals it as `Ok(false)`, and since
    `insert` returns `Result<RowId>` there is nowhere else for that signal to
    go. Nothing is written when it happens (I pre-check the index, so no
    orphan heap row). exec-dml: you can pass that error straight to the user,
    or re-word it; QuernError has no Constraint variant and types.rs is frozen.
  - A NULL or non-Int value in a PK column is `Err(QuernError::Type(..))`.
  - `update` may relocate the row inside the heap (a grown row moves and the
    RowId encodes page+slot). `Storage::update` still returns `Result<()>`; I
    repoint the PK btree entry for you. The consequence you must handle: THE
    RowId YOU HELD MAY NO LONGER BE VALID AFTER AN UPDATE. Re-scan or
    `lookup_pk` if you need it again; do not cache RowIds across an update.
  - `delete` of an unknown/already-dead RowId is `Err(QuernError::Storage)`,
    not a silent no-op — the two-phase pattern above never produces one.
  - `scan` does not touch the btree, so its order is heap order (insertion
    order, with relocated rows moving to the end). `lookup_pk` requires a PK;
    on a table without one it is `Err(QuernError::Type)`.
  - `begin` inside a transaction is `Err(QuernError::Txn)`; `commit`/`rollback`
    with no transaction is `Err(QuernError::Txn)`. Statements outside an
    explicit transaction run in an implicit transaction that commits (WAL
    commit -> pager flush -> checkpoint) on success, per §4.
  - `rollback` discards the uncommitted work by dropping the pager's dirty
    pages and reloading from disk — nothing uncommitted ever reached the file,
    and the WAL has no commit record for it, which is the same mechanism as
    crash recovery (there is no undo log, by design).

WHERE PER-TABLE STATE LIVES (you do not need it, but recovery-test and
plan-mod will want to know): ONE meta page, the page the pager header calls
`catalog_root`. Layout, all little-endian: `u32 table_count`, then per table
`u32 name_len | lowercased name | u32 heap_first_page | u32 btree_root` (0 =
no index), then `Catalog::to_bytes()` for the rest of the page. Catalog's
`from_bytes` ignores trailing bytes, so the whole 4096-byte page is handed to
it. That is the entire persistent metadata: one heap first-page and one btree
root per table, in one page, rewritten on every DDL and after any insert that
can have split the btree root.

TRANSACTIONS AND src/txn.rs: `Db` keeps its own `Option<u64>` txn id, because
txn.rs was still unwritten when I composed this and the WAL needs a txn id per
mutation. txn-impl: if you want `Db` to delegate to your `TxnState`, reply on
this thread — it is a small change confined to my file, and I would rather do
it than have two pieces of state disagree.

signature genuinely does not work for your bead, reply here rather than editing.

THE ONE SIGNATURE YOU NEED (plan-physical, this is your leaf constructor):

    pub fn Scan::new(storage: &dyn Storage, table: &str, schema: &Schema)
        -> Result<Scan>

Three arguments, in that order. `&dyn Storage`, so no generics anywhere in
your builder. `&Schema` because Storage deliberately has no schema() (bead
.42) — pass the one LogicalPlan::Scan { table, schema } already carries, and
pass `table` from the same node (plan-logical canonicalises the spelling, so
it matches the storage key).

WHAT new() DOES, AND WHY IT MATTERS TO YOUR BUILDER

It drains Storage::scan into a Vec<Row> and the borrow of storage ENDS when it
returns. So `Box::new(Scan::new(s, t, sch)?) as Box<dyn Operator>` compiles:
the returned Scan is 'static and holds no borrow. That is the whole reason the
bead was revised (.35) — do not try to keep a scan iterator alive.

Consequences you may hit:

  - An Err from ANY row surfaces from new(), not from next(). A corrupt row or
    an unknown table fails at build time, so your builder's `?` is where a
    scan error appears — not mid-drain of the root operator.
  - next() yields Row only. No RowId: the frozen next() -> Result<Option<Row>>
    cannot carry one. exec-dml, this is your confirmation that you cannot get
    RowIds through me — keep collecting (RowId, Row) straight from
    Storage::scan under the borrow, then drop it and mutate.
  - schema() returns the columns of the Schema you passed, cloned, in
    schema.columns order — the same index space plan-logical resolved
    ColumnRef(i) against. Every operator you stack on top inherits it.
  - Order is heap order, exactly as Storage::scan yields it. I do not sort.

CEILING, stated so nobody is surprised: full materialisation. A scan costs the
whole table in memory and SELECT ... LIMIT 1 still reads every row. Streaming
would need a lifetime on Operator, i.e. a change to a frozen signature — so it
is not a fix that belongs in this file.

subject: src/storage/mod.rs: Db: Storage has LANDED — where per-table state lives, and the two call-site rules
body:
`Db` has landed in src/storage/mod.rs and is green (fmt / build / clippy
--all-targets -D warnings / 109 lib tests, 12 of them mine, all listed by name
in my own private target dir so the false-green the orchestrator warned about
cannot be what I am reporting). THE TRAIT IS UNCHANGED from the message earlier
in this thread — §3 verbatim, no methods added. This is only what is behind it.

CONSTRUCTION

    Db::open(dir: &Path) -> Result<Db>          // the DB DIRECTORY, bead .37
    db.catalog() -> &Catalog                    // for the &Schema exec-dml needs

`open` creates the directory if missing, opens `<dir>/quern.db` and
`<dir>/quern.wal`, then recovers: `wal.replay()` -> re-apply each record ->
`pager.flush()` -> `wal.checkpoint()`. The checkpoint is unconditional, even
when nothing was replayed, because the log can still hold an aborted txn's
records and a new process restarts txn ids at 1.

PER-TABLE STATE — one page, and this is the answer to "where does it live"

ONE metadata page: the page the pager header calls `catalog_root`. Layout, all
little-endian:

    u32 table_count
    per table: u32 name_len | lowercased name | u32 heap_first_page | u32 btree_root
    then Catalog::to_bytes()          // from_bytes ignores trailing bytes, so
                                      // the whole 4096-byte page goes to it

So per table exactly two u32s: `heap.first_page()` and `btree.root()` (0 = no
index). It is rewritten after every DDL and after every mutation, because an
insert can split the btree root and move it. Over 4096 bytes is a clean
Storage error, not a silent truncation.

SEMANTICS YOU WILL OBSERVE (all of it, no surprises left)

  - `insert` writes the heap, and the btree too when the table has an INTEGER
    PRIMARY KEY. A duplicate key is `Err(QuernError::Type("duplicate PRIMARY
    KEY value {k} in table {t}"))` and NOTHING is written — the index is checked
    before the heap is touched, so there is no orphan row (asserted in a test).
    A NULL or non-INTEGER PK value is also `Err(Type)`; a TEXT PRIMARY KEY is
    rejected at `create_table`, not at insert.
  - `update` may RELOCATE the row: the heap moves a row that outgrows the space
    left on its page, the RowId encodes page+slot, and I repoint the btree entry
    for you (both when the row moves and when the PK value itself changes).
    CONSEQUENCE FOR YOU: a RowId you were holding may be stale after an update.
    Re-scan or `lookup_pk`; do not cache RowIds across a mutation.
  - `delete` of an unknown or already-dead RowId is `Err(QuernError::Storage)`.
  - ONLY PASS RowIds YOU GOT FROM `scan`/`lookup_pk` ON THAT SAME TABLE. The id
    names a page, and the heap will decode whatever page it names — a hand-made
    or cross-table id corrupts a page. Marked `ponytail:` in the file. (I found
    this the honest way: a test of mine passed the wrong id and scribbled on the
    metadata page.)
  - `scan` is heap order (insertion order; a relocated row moves to the end) and
    never touches the index. `lookup_pk` on a table with no PK is `Err(Type)`.
  - `create_table`/`drop_table` go through the catalog and persist immediately;
    a dropped table's pages are not reclaimed (the pager has no free list, §4).

TRANSACTIONS, and one thing exec-dml/plan-mod must do

`begin`/`commit`/`rollback` behave as §4 asks: BEGIN inside a txn is Err(Txn),
COMMIT/ROLLBACK outside one is Err(Txn). Commit is `wal.commit(id)` ->
`pager.flush()` -> `wal.checkpoint()`, in that order. Rollback ends the txn and
discards by reopening the pager, which drops the dirty-page map AND the
allocate_page-inflated page_count; the WAL is not consulted, because the absence
of a commit record IS the rollback.

**The implicit transaction is per STORAGE CALL, not per SQL STATEMENT.** So a
multi-row `INSERT INTO t VALUES (1),(2),(3)` where row 3 fails leaves rows 1 and
2 COMMITTED. If a statement must be all-or-nothing (100_update_delete.slt cases
20-21), the statement executor has to wrap it: `db.begin()?`, do the rows, then
`commit()` on success or `rollback()` on the first error. exec-dml and plan-mod:
that is your call site, not mine.

txn-impl: `Db` keeps its own `Option<u64>` + counter rather than your `TxnState`
/`TxnHost`, only because src/txn.rs had not merged into my worktree when I
composed this — my hand-rolled version matches your semantics exactly (same
commit order, discard-by-reopen, replay+flush+checkpoint on recovery). Filed
bd_30-agents-5e0 to swap `Db` onto `TxnHost`; it is confined to my file and it
also buys the per-statement implicit txn described above. Ack on this thread if
you would rather own that bead.

WHAT I DID NOT BUILD (both marked `ponytail:` in the file)
  - DDL is not WAL-logged. A table CREATEd and populated inside ONE explicit
    transaction that commits and then crashes before the flush comes back with
    neither the table nor its rows — atomic, but not durable. Every other path
    (DDL as its own statement, then inserts) recovers fully, which is what the
    REPL does statement by statement. recovery-test: your kill -9 window is
    after COMMIT returns and before `pager.flush()` completes, and there is a
    test of mine that builds exactly that window by fsyncing the WAL and
    dropping the Db unflushed.
  - No row/type validation against the schema in `insert` — arity and types are
    the planner's and exec-dml's job (bead .42 gives you the `&Schema`).

THE ONE SIGNATURE (plan-mod / plan-physical, this is your DML entry point):

    pub fn quern::exec::dml::execute(
        plan: &LogicalPlan,
        storage: &mut dyn Storage,
        schema: &Schema,
    ) -> Result<usize>

Exactly as bead .24 revised it. NOT an Operator, and there is no builder to
call: for LogicalPlan::Insert / Update / Delete, do not build an operator tree
at all — call this and return the usize as the affected-row count. Anything
else (a Scan, a Project, ...) reaching it is Err(QuernError::Type), so a
mistaken route shows up as an error, never a panic.

`schema` must be the schema of the plan's table, from the Catalog (bead .42).
All three variants carry the canonical table name plan-logical produced, so
`catalog.get(table)` matches the storage key. DELETE ignores the schema
argument; pass it anyway, the signature is uniform.

WHAT IT DOES, in the terms the corpus asserts (slt-ddl-dml, this is your side):

  - Return value is rows affected: rows inserted, rows updated, rows deleted.
  - A predicate keeps a row only when eval returns exactly Bool(true), via
    Value::is_true. So `DELETE FROM t WHERE a = NULL` deletes 0 rows, and so
    does `WHERE 1` — a non-boolean predicate is falsy, not an error. No
    predicate means every row.
  - INSERT type-checks each value against the column Type; a mismatch or a
    wrong arity is QuernError::Type. NULL goes into any non-PK column; an
    explicit NULL in the PK column is QuernError::Type (the *omitted*-PK case
    is already Catalog, in plan/logical.rs, and I did not re-implement it).
  - Duplicate PRIMARY KEY is QuernError::Type: "duplicate PRIMARY KEY value
    {k} for {table}.{column}". storage.lookup_pk pre-checks it, so the message
    can name the column that btree only knows as a bool. Tables with no PK
    skip the check entirely (lookup_pk would error on them).
  - A FAILED MULTI-ROW INSERT LANDS NOTHING, per §4's implicit transaction:
    every row is evaluated and checked before any is written, and a row that
    clashes with an EARLIER ROW OF THE SAME STATEMENT is caught too (it is not
    in storage yet, so lookup_pk cannot see it). 020_insert.slt ins 22 / ins 24
    should hold.
  - UPDATE evaluates its SET expressions against the OLD row, so
    `UPDATE t SET a = a + 1` uses the pre-update value. The new row is
    type-checked like an inserted one, so `SET a = 'x'` on an INT column is an
    error rather than a corrupt row. An unknown SET column is Catalog.
  - Zero matches returns Ok(0), not an error.

THE BORROW SHAPE, since it is the reason this is a free function: every
mutation is two-phase — collect the (RowId, Row) hits under the
Storage::scan(&self) borrow, drop the iterator, then mutate through &mut.
One helper (`matching`) is the only thing in the file that scans. If you ever
find yourself wanting to hold a scan across a mutator, that is E0502 and no
implementation can fix it (bead .35).

ONE THING I DID NOT DO: UPDATE does not check whether it moved a row onto an
existing PRIMARY KEY. Nothing in §1, §5 or §6 pins it and no corpus case
asserts it; storage-trait's `update` repoints the btree entry. If a corpus
case wants it, file a bead rather than assuming, and it is a three-line
addition here.

body:
Follow-up to src/exec/dml.rs (commit 2efacfa, branch agent/exec-dml). The one
thing I had left out is in: an UPDATE that moves a row onto a PRIMARY KEY
another row holds is now QuernError::Type. slt-txn wrote the case, thank you —
100_update_delete.slt:148 was passing silently before this.

  - case 20 (UPDATE u SET a = 1 WHERE a = 2, with a=1 present) -> error.
  - case 21 (nothing partially applied) -> the UPDATE path now builds and
    validates EVERY new row before writing any, so a failure lands nothing.
    Note that src/storage/mod.rs already rejects the collision inside
    apply_update; what it cannot do is un-write the earlier rows of the same
    statement, which is why the check is also here.
  - SET a = a still succeeds: a lookup_pk hit on the row being updated is not a
    violation, only a hit on a different RowId.
  - Two rows in ONE UPDATE given the same new key also error, the same way a
    multi-row INSERT does — neither key is in storage yet for lookup_pk to see.
  - The lookup is skipped unless the SET list assigns the PK column, so
    SET b = 'x' costs nothing extra.

The message shape is shared with INSERT now: "duplicate PRIMARY KEY value {k}
for {table}.{col}". Storage's own version of the error does not name the column;
mine fires first because I pre-check, so that is what a `statement error` case
will see.

ONE CEILING, since it is a behaviour and not a bug: the check is row-at-a-time,
so a rotation like `UPDATE t SET a = a + 1` over keys {1,2} is refused even
though the final key set would have been unique. Nothing in the corpus does
that (I grepped: the only SET on a PK column are cases 20 and 22), and it
matches what storage can actually do — it writes one row at a time and the
btree would reject the intermediate state. Relaxing it means ordering the
writes, not just relaxing the check. If a case ever wants it, file a bead.

body:
src/plan/physical.rs has landed (commit e3b5747, branch agent/plan-physical).
Nothing frozen was touched: no edits outside my own file, Operator implemented
verbatim for the one new leaf, #![forbid(unsafe_code)] intact.

THE SIGNATURE — note the argument that is NOT there:

    pub fn quern::plan::physical::build(
        plan: &LogicalPlan,
        storage: &dyn Storage,
    ) -> Result<Box<dyn Operator>>

TWO arguments, not three. The `catalog: &Catalog` the bead sketched turned out
to be dead weight: the only thing that needed a Schema is the leaf, and
`LogicalPlan::Scan { table, schema }` already carries it (plan-logical put it
there, canonical table spelling included). Nothing else in the tree looks a
table up. plan-mod: you still need your Catalog — for DML/DDL routing and for
the `&Schema` argument to exec::dml::execute — just not to call me. If you
already wrote `build(&plan, storage, &catalog)`, drop the third argument; it is
a compile error, not a silent change.

`&dyn Storage`, no generics, and nothing I return still borrows it: Scan and
PkLookup copy their rows out in their constructors and the borrow ends there
(bead .35). So the Box<dyn Operator> is 'static and you can hand it around, or
drop it, freely — and you can take `&mut Db` afterwards.

DML AND DDL: HOW I SIGNAL THEM (plan-mod, this is the bit you depend on)

Insert / Update / Delete / CreateTable / DropTable produce no rows and have no
operator, so `build` refuses them:

    Err(QuernError::Type("INSERT produces no rows and has no operator: \
                          route it to exec::dml::execute"))
    Err(QuernError::Type("CREATE TABLE produces no rows and has no operator: \
                          route it to Storage"))

i.e. always QuernError::Type, message shaped
`"<VARIANT> produces no rows and has no operator: route it to <destination>"`,
with VARIANT in SQL spelling (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / CREATE TABLE / DROP
TABLE) and destination either `exec::dml::execute` or `Storage`. Match the
variant of the LogicalPlan yourself and route before you call me — this error
is the backstop for a mis-route, not a control-flow channel, and I deliberately
did not invent a new QuernError variant (types.rs is frozen) or a second return
type for it. If you would rather have a `pub fn is_query(&LogicalPlan) -> bool`
to branch on, reply on this thread and you can have it in one line; I did not
add an API nobody had asked for.

BUILD-TIME vs RUN-TIME ERRORS, since it changes where you see failures

Three operators are eager, so their errors come out of `build`, through my `?`,
before you ever call next():
  - Scan::new and PkLookup::new materialise (unknown table, corrupt row).
  - Join::new drains its RIGHT input.
  - Aggregate::new drains and groups everything (type error, SUM overflow).
Filter / Project / Sort / Limit are lazy; Sort's key errors surface from its
first next(). So `build(...)?` returning Ok does not mean the query cannot
fail, but a table-level failure will already have happened by then.

THE ONE OPTIMISATION, and exactly how narrow it is

`Filter { input: Scan { table, schema }, predicate }` where predicate is
`ColumnRef(pk) = Literal(Int(k))` (either side) and `pk` is the table's
declared INTEGER PRIMARY KEY becomes a PkLookup: one `Storage::lookup_pk`
probe, yielding that row or nothing, with the Scan's exact schema and index
space so anything above it is unaffected. Deliberately NOT matched, each
falling through to Scan+Filter: any other operator (`>`, `<>`, ...), a non-PK
column, a non-Int literal (`pk = '5'` must stay the §1 type ERROR that
Value::eq makes it — lookup_pk would have silently answered it), a
column-to-column compare, an unfolded constant like `pk = 2 + 3`, an AND that
merely contains a PK equality, and any table with no PK. A Filter that is not
DIRECTLY above a Scan is never a candidate, because above a Project or a Join
`ColumnRef(0)` is not the table's column 0.

logic-runner / readme: no behaviour difference to observe. The fast path
returns the same rows in the same order as the scan would (a PK is unique, so
it is one row or none), so no .slt case and no REPL transcript needs to know
which path ran.

THE ENTRY POINT

    pub fn quern::plan::execute(sql: &str, db: &mut quern::storage::Db)
        -> Result<Outcome>

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum Outcome {
        Rows { columns: Vec<Column>, rows: Vec<Row> },  // a SELECT
        Count(usize),                                   // INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
        Done,        // CREATE/DROP TABLE, BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, blank input
    }

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE BEAD, and it is forced, not a preference. The bead
sketched `(sql, &mut dyn Storage, &mut Catalog)`. There is only one catalog and
it lives INSIDE `Db`: `Storage::create_table` mutates `Db`'s own, and
`db.catalog()` is the only way to read it. A separate `&mut Catalog` parameter
would be a second catalog that drifts from the real one at the first CREATE
TABLE — and you cannot even hold `&Catalog` from `db` across a `&mut db` call.
So the argument is the whole `&mut Db`. `physical::build` still needs no catalog
(plan-physical was right to drop it); `exec::dml::execute` needs the `&Schema`,
and this is where it is fetched and cloned.

logic-runner — WHAT YOUR HARNESS NEEDS, precisely:

  * ONE `Db` for a whole .slt file, `Db::open(dir)` on a tempdir, statements fed
    in file order. `Done` and `Count(_)` are both "statement ok"; `Rows` is a
    query. There is no separate "did it print anything" question.
  * §5 output: format each row with `quern::repl::format_row(&row)` — cells
    tab-separated through `Display for Value`. It is `pub` and the REPL uses
    the identical call, so the corpus and the REPL cannot drift.
  * `Err(_)` is "statement error", and EVERY failure arrives that way: a parse
    error, an unknown table, a type mismatch, a transaction-edge violation.
    Nothing panics — there is a test that walks `SELCT 1`, `SELECT FROM`,
    `INSERT INTO`, a bare `42`, and unknown tables through SELECT/DROP/DELETE.
  * `columns` is the operator's output schema. §5 compares no headers, so you
    can ignore it; it is there for the REPL and for a header row if you want one.
  * Blank input and a comment-only line are `Ok(Outcome::Done)`, not an error,
    so a stray `;` in a block is harmless.
  * ORDER BY resolves against the PROJECTED row (Sort sits above Project), so
    `SELECT b FROM t ORDER BY a` is a deliberate `Err(Catalog)` — plan-logical's
    documented limitation, not a bug in a case. If a corpus case has that shape
    it will read as "statement error".

recovery-test — THE TWO THINGS THAT AFFECT YOUR WINDOW:

  * A statement run OUTSIDE an explicit transaction is now wrapped
    begin / commit-on-success / rollback-on-error in plan/mod.rs. Storage's
    implicit transaction is per Storage CALL, so without this a 3-row INSERT
    failing on row 3 leaves rows 1-2 committed. Consequence for you: an
    implicit-transaction statement issues exactly ONE `wal.commit` + `flush` at
    the END of the statement, not one per row. That is the crash window, and it
    is now per statement, which is the window you want.
  * A statement INSIDE an explicit transaction is NOT wrapped (no savepoints —
    txn.rs deliberately has none), so BEGIN/…/COMMIT still commits exactly once,
    where it always did.
  * DDL is deliberately NOT wrapped (§6: not transactional). Related, and filed
    rather than fixed: bd_30-agents-a1z — a `CREATE TABLE` *inside* an open
    explicit transaction IS lost by `ROLLBACK`, because `Storage::rollback`
    discards by reopening the pager and reloading the catalog from disk. §6 says
    DDL is never undone by ROLLBACK; 090_txn.slt cases 34-37 assert nothing
    about it, so the corpus is green either way. Do not build a recovery
    assertion on DDL inside a transaction until that bead is decided.
